gen-metal-mania-instrument-sans: Instrument Sans draws its pincer-like openings and its stroke at a single weight, so lines read crisp and modern. Metal Mania hammers in above it, intense and heavy.
gen-metal-mania-inter: Inter keeps its lines smooth and tube-like, with big counters in a tall lowercase. Down a whole page it reads easily and quietly, a plain sans letting Metal Mania's bent-paperclip strokes do the shouting above.
gen-metal-mania-mulish: Mulish reads soft and approachable, its apertures open like a horseshoe magnet and its strokes free of any thick-and-thin shift. Metal Mania's dense, heavy intensity is what makes the contrast stand out.
gen-metal-mania-poppins: Intense, heavy Metal Mania gets the top spot, its eyes large and its text packed tight. It hits hardest in big dramatic lines, while Poppins brings loose, rope-like curves and a tall, sturdy sans body.
gen-metal-mania-roboto-slab: Jagged and dense, Metal Mania has strokes like bent paperclips and a heavy, intense presence. It delivers the punch, while Roboto Slab gives precise, structured slab-serif text with open throats.
gen-modak-instrument-sans: Instrument Sans has open pincer-like curves and a steady stroke, giving a clean, modern texture in a minimal-step lowercase. Modak's fun, puffy letters sit above it and loosen the whole look.
gen-modak-mulish: Modak has fun, approachable letters with big washer-like eyes and strokes that never thin out, and Mulish backs it up. The heading brings the cheerful bulk, but the sans body brings a large x-height and short ascenders.
gen-modak-poppins: Chunky and cheerful, Modak plays with huge lowercase eyes and a c that stays wide open. And Poppins follows in a plain sans with rope-loose curves and a tall, sturdy body that steadies the page.
gen-newsreader-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans reads sharp and refined, leaving generous space between its curve ends and the stem, and its lines stay crisp. Newsreader does the journalistic, literary voice best, while the sans-serif body keeps things tidy.
gen-nosifer-bitter: Dark, commanding Nosifer pinches its mouths shut like a sealed envelope flap, with a widely tracked rhythm. And Bitter does the opposite, a dependable slab-serif with a very large lowercase eye and open s shapes.
